To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we are able to estimate trajectory and pose using range and inertia sensors and the results are comparable to wheel odometry.
the trajectory estimation is improved by using the IMU sensor data and the pose estimation is improved by the use of the IMU sensor and kinematic data.
the use of the inertial sensors improves both the SLAM and the iterative closest point methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of algorithms for the estimation of robot trajectories and poses in unknown environments based on range and inertial data.
the following questions: How does the trajectory estimation accuracy depend on the number of range sensors?
the following questions: How to improve the performance of the SLAM algorithm by using inertial sensor and kinematic data?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methods can be used in a variety of applications such as mobile robotics, autonomous vehicles and autonomous navigation in unknown environments.
the SLAM based gMapping approach with the use of inertial sensor is the best approach in this thesis for the trajectory and pose estimation of the mobile robots.
the proposed methods have shown promising results in the estimation of trajectory and pose of a robot.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully implemented the gMapping and LSM algorithms for pose estimation and trajectory estimation.
the use of the IMU sensor improves the accuracy of the trajectory and pose estimations in both the SLAM and the LSM approaches.
the trajectory and pose estimation using LSM with the use of IMU sensor is more robust than gMapping.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the trajectory and pose estimation can be done with range sensors without the use of wheel odometry and that the use of an inertial measurement unit (IMU) can improve the trajectory and pose estimations.
the use of inertial sensors can be used to increase accuracy and reduce computational time for trajectory and pose estimates.
, the use of inertial sensor improves the performance of SLAM based gMapping and LSM based laser scan matcher significantly.
